findings: The account's core extends/implements constructor-order claim is supported by Java CommandCreateClassMultilines.manageExtends and by both held-out comma-separated matrices. Java iterates each target, creates a missing parent if needed, then constructs its Link before advancing; Rust's event stream matches those cases.

The account is incomplete for association-class events. AbstractClassOrObjectDiagram.Association.createNew consumes six slots only when no A-B link exists: apoint short name, point Entity, temporary A-B Link, and three emitted Links. When an A-B link already exists, Java removes it and skips the temporary Link, consuming five slots. Rust records only Association(index), hardcodes ASSOCIATION_SEQUENCE_SLOTS = 6, and does not encode or apply base-link replacement.

The paired association cases isolate that branch. The no-base control is structurally equivalent. The preexisting-base case shifts every association link and subsequent entity/link by one and leaves the base link in Rust output, directly disproving the claimed general replay model.

The relevant constant has an adjacent provenance comment, but that comment incorrectly generalizes the no-base branch to all associations. This is an unexplained parity constant in effect because its asserted Java derivation omits the foundLink(existingLink) branch at AbstractClassOrObjectDiagram.java:250-257.

Left/up links survive the held-out transient-constructor check. Java Link.getInv constructs a replacement Link and consumes a second UID; Rust's inverted relationship allocation reproduces that sequence.

Attached-note UID allocation itself matches Java in the note/link matrix, including GMN3/ent0004 and GMN11/ent0012, but Rust emits generated note entities after all ordinary entities. That downstream document-order failure independently fails the required no-oracle perturbation gate.

The two qualified-package matrices fail only on a repeated 1.0011 px horizontal package-shell/title offset. They do not disprove UID allocation, but they are preserved because the required shipped-path no-oracle comparator rejected them.

Static inspection found no changed include_str/include_bytes use, filesystem golden reads, test-diagram reads, fixture-label production conditionals, coordinate-keyed SVG surgery, or per-fixture branch-count ladder in the mechanism diff. Test labels occur only in tests. The rejection rests on a genuine missing Java branch and a counterexample, not fixture-shaped logic.
All nine Java SVGs are well-formed XML and contain no recognized PlantUML error marker. Each final source hash occurs exactly once in the repository's PlantUML corpus.
rejection_basis: checker_association_then_relation is a valid fresh counterexample to the shared UID replay model, and three additional fresh inputs also fail the mandatory no-oracle comparator
